title: What I learned building my first IoT project
excerpt: The laundry scheduler taught me more about systems thinking than any textbook. Here's what went sideways and why I'm glad it did.
html:
Nobody tells you that IoT projects spend 80% of their time not working. The device is unresponsive. The API returns nothing. The socket drops out every 12 minutes for no reason anyone can explain.

This is the laundry scheduler project I'm building for a course — an IoT-connected smart socket that monitors power draw, detects when a wash cycle finishes, and schedules the next run automatically via a web dashboard.

What actually happened

Week 1: I underestimated how much of the work is just getting devices to talk to each other reliably. Not even doing anything useful — just talking.

Week 2: I overbuilt the dashboard. Spent two days on UI that nobody asked for before realising the core sensor logic wasn't working yet.

Week 3: I stripped everything back. One endpoint. One sensor read. One display. Got that working first, then built outward.

The real lesson

Systems thinking over feature building. I kept wanting to add things before the foundation was solid. Once I stopped doing that, the project moved fast.

The other lesson: debugging across hardware and software simultaneously is genuinely hard and genuinely satisfying when you nail it.

More updates as the project develops.
